Let me analyze this OIML certificate for a water meter.

Key data:
- Certificate: R49/2013-A-SK1-2023.01
- Scheme: A
- Member state: Slovakia
- Issuing authority: Slovak Legal Metrology (SLM), Hviezdoslavova 1124/31, 974 01 Banská Bystrica, Slovakia, Peter Vook, Director
- Applicant: Huizhong Instrumentation Co., Ltd., No.126 West Gaoxin Road, High-Tech Industrial Development Zone, Tangshan 063020, China
- Manufacturer: same as applicant
- Certified type: Water meter type 100E / SCL-61H-100 (two alternative names type)
- Module: Ultrasonic water meter with electronic indication device
- Recommendation: R49, Edition 2013, accuracy class 2
- Date issued: 13th January 2023
- Type evaluation report: No. 2023/ER001/SK1, dated 13 January 2023, 17 pages
- Documentation file: "Technical documentation file Huizhong_100E_00", 13 January 2023, 150 pages
- Revision history: Revision 0, 13 January 2023, "Certificate first issued"
- Project number: FK-P05-85? That's a form code probably. Page total: 8 pages. Hmm, project number — the footer "FK-P05-85" is a form number. Not clearly a project number. I'll omit it or maybe not include. The schema has project_number; not clearly present. Skip.

Models: The certificate covers DN15, DN20, DN25, DN32, DN40 variants (5 sizes). Model family: water meter 100E / SCL-61H-100.

Table 1 (DN15, 20, 25):

- Ratio Q2/Q1: -: 1.6 (all)

- Installation orientation: H/V with indication device on top

Common characteristics (type_level):
- Water temperature range: 0.1 to 50 °C (temperature classes T30, T50)
- MAP: 16 bar

- MPE upper range: ±2% (at Θ ≤ 30°C), ±3% (at Θ>30°C)
- MPE lower range: ±5%

- Scale interval: 0.00001 m³
- Accuracy class: 2
- Mechanical class: M1
- Climatic class: -25 to +70 °C
- Electromagnetic class: E2
- Environmental conditions class: O (fixed meters installed outdoors)
- Flow profile sensitivity class: U0D0
- Battery: non-replaceable li-battery 3.6 V, life time 13 years

Dimensions table (Fig 2a):
- DN15: L1=110/165, L=97, H=119, W=98, A=G ¾ B
- DN20: L1=130/154/190/195, L=97, H=119, W=98, A=G 1B
- DN25: L1=160/225/260, L=97, H=119, W=98, A=G 1 ¼ B
Fig 2b:
- DN32: L1=180, L=97, H=145, W=98, A=G 1 ½ B
- DN40: L1=200/245/300, L=97, H=153, W=98, A=G 2B

Wait, in the Fig 2a table, L, H, W have rowspan=3 with values 97, 119, 98. In Fig 2b, L rowspan=2 = 97, H is 145 for DN32 and 153 for DN40, W rowspan=2 = 98.

Note: "L" here of 97 seems odd given construction lengths of 110-260... Actually "L" might be a drawing dimension; but I'll preserve matrix tables.

Software versions: V1-1.1 with checksums 3651 (NB-IoT), 10200 (NB-IoT with pressure sensor), 65167 (RS 485). Could include as a matrix table or components info.

Model family: family_name "100E / SCL-61H-100", models with model_id per DN: "DN15", "DN20", "DN25", "DN32", "DN40".

Model-level characteristics:
- nominal_dn: mm: 15, 20, 25, 32, 40
- permanent_flowrate_q3: m³/h: 2.5, 4, 6.3, 10, 16
- minimum_flowrate_q1: m³/h: 0.006, 0.01, 0.016, 0.025, 0.04
- transitional_flowrate_q2: m³/h: 0.01, 0.016, 0.025, 0.04, 0.064
- overload_flowrate_q4: m³/h: 3.125, 5, 7.875, 12.5, 20
- ratio_q3_q1: dimensionless: 400 (same for all — could be type_level with value 400, unit null; the unit column says "R". Hmm, "R" as unit — it's a ratio designation R400. I'll use value 400 with unit_symbol null, or "R". Actually ratio Q3/Q1 = R 400. The unit column shows "R". I could put unit_symbol: "R"? Better to keep value 400 and treat as dimensionless ratio; attribute name conveys it. I'll set unit_symbol null.)
- ratio_q2_q1: 1.6 for all → type_level
- connection_thread: "G ¾ B", "G1 B", "G1 ¼ B", "G 1 ½ B", "G2 B" → model_level string values (structured values allow strings)
- construction_length: mm: lists "110/165" etc. These are lists of alternative lengths. Value could be a string "110/165" or a list. Schema says value can be number | {min,max} | string. Multiple discrete values — hmm. For construction length, these are alternatives. I could keep as string "110/165". Or use matrix_tables to preserve. I'll keep model_level with string values, and also matrix_tables for dimensions.

Actually the schema allows value to be a string. "110/165" is a list of options; keeping string is fine. Alternatively, arrays are not allowed per shape. Keep strings.

- installation_orientation: "H/V" — same for all → type_level string value "H/V with indication device on top".

Type-level characteristics:
- water_temperature_range: {min: 0.1, max: 50} °C
- temperature_classes: "T30, T50" → string
- maximum_admissible_pressure_map: 16 bar
- pressure_loss: 0.63 bar
- pressure_loss_class: "Δp 63" → string "Δp63" (avoid LaTeX — Δ is fine? Rule says no LaTeX; Δ is a Unicode char, fine.)
- max_permitted_error_upper_flowrates: ±2% at ≤30°C and ±3% at >30°C — this varies by temperature condition → config_level! Axis: "water_temperature". Values: {condition: "Θ ≤ 30 °C", value: ±2...}. Value ±2 — sign matters. Could encode value as string "±2"? Or {min: -2, max: 2}. Hmm. MPE is ±2%. I'd use value: {"min": -2, "max": 2}? That could be misread. Simpler: string "±2". The rules say numbers not strings for numbers, but ±2 isn't a plain number. I'll use {min: -2, max: 2} with unit %... Actually for MPE that's standard interpretation: error within ±2%. I'll use {min:-2, max:2}. Hmm, but some might prefer string. Let me think: The rule for ranges says "0-9.999" → {min, max}. "±2" is symmetric range → {min:-2, max:2} seems reasonable. I'll do that.
- max_permitted_error_lower_flowrates: ±5 → {min:-5, max:5} %
- calculator_capacity / maximum_indication_range: 99999.99999 m³
- scale_interval: 0.00001 m³
- accuracy_class: 2
- mechanical_class: "M1"
- climatic_class_range: {min:-25, max:70} °C (climatic class is usually denoted by temp range; class value "-25 to +70" — climatic class in OIML R49 is given as temperature range. Keep as climatic_class with range.)
- electromagnetic_class: "E2"
- environmental_conditions_class: "O" with note "fixed meters installed outdoors"
- flow_profile_sensitivity_class: "U0D0"
- battery_voltage: 3.6 V
- battery_life: 13 years
- battery_type: "non-replaceable lithium battery"
- battery_life_end_indicator_threshold: 3.6 V (from description: "activated when the battery voltage is below 3,6 V")

Config-level:
- max_permitted_error_upper_flowrates by temperature: axis "water_temperature": conditions "Θ ≤ 30 °C" → ±2, "Θ > 30 °C" → ±3.

Components:
- Flow sensor: cylindrical brass body... role "flow_sensor"
- Calculator and indication device: role "calculator_and_indication_device"
- Non-essential: pressure sensor, thermistor — could include with role and essential: false? Schema doesn't have essential flag but characteristics{} free-form. I'll include them.

Test reports:
- id: "2023/ER001/SK1", date: 2023-01-13, pages: 17, role: "type_evaluation_report"
- documentation file: "Technical documentation file Huizhong_100E_00", date 2023-01-13, pages 150, role "documentation_file"

Revision history:
- revision "0", date "2023-01-13", changes "Certificate first issued"

Footnotes: none present. Omit.

Dates: date_issued: "2023-01-13". Page total: 8.

Scheme: A.

OIML issuer id: not given explicitly (SK1 appears in cert number and report number). The schema has oiml_issuer_id at certificate level. Not clearly stated; the issuing authority identifier "SK1" appears in cert number R49/2013-A-SK1-2023.01. I could set oiml_issuer_id: "SK1". Hmm — rule 8 says don't fabricate. SK1 is plausibly the issuer identifier. I'll include "SK1" as it's derived from the certificate number, arguably. Actually, safer to include since it's in the cert number; but it's an inference. I'll omit from certificate level but mention? The schema lists oiml_issuer_id for both certificate and issuing_authority. I'll include "SK1" — it's a reasonable extraction from "2023/ER001/SK1" and cert number. Hmm, risk of fabrication. I think including "SK1" is defensible but I'll leave it out to be safe? The rules: "If a field is not present in the markdown, omit it." SK1 is present in the markdown but not labeled as issuer id. I'll omit.

Recommendation: id "R49", edition 2013, amendment null, scheme "A", accuracy_classes ["2"].

Matrix tables:
1. "Table 1 – Technical and metrological data (DN15–DN25)" — columns: characteristic, unit, DN15, DN20, DN25. Rows as objects. I'll build rows per characteristic with values.

Actually the R137 example shows columns as attributes and rows per model. Let me do that: columns ["nominal_dn", "permanent_flowrate_q3", "minimum_flowrate_q1", "transitional_flowrate_q2", "overload_flowrate_q4", "ratio_q3_q1", "ratio_q2_q1", "connection_thread", "construction_length", "installation_orientation"], rows: {"nominal_dn": 15, "permanent_flowrate_q3": 2.5, ...}. Units in column_units.

Table 2 similar for DN32, DN40.

Combine into one matrix_table "Technical and metrological data by nominal diameter" with all 5 rows? The doc splits into Table 1 and Table 2, but shared characteristics repeat. I could make one matrix table with 5 rows, or two. I'll make two to preserve document structure, or one combined for clarity. I'll do one combined "Technical and metrological data (Tables 1 and 2)" with 5 rows — cleaner. Hmm, but preserve doc structure... The example combined a single table. Two tables is more faithful. I'll do two matrix_tables: table_1 and table_2. Also a dimensions table.

Dimensions tables (Fig 2a and 2b): columns: type, dn, l1, l, h, w, a. Rows:
Fig 2a: {dn:15, l1:"110/165", l:97, h:119, w:98, a:"G ¾ B"}, {dn:20,...}, {dn:25,...}
Fig 2b: {dn:32, l1:180, l:97, h:145, w:98, a:"G 1 ½ B"}, {dn:40, l1:"200/245/300", l:97, h:153, w:98, a:"G2 B"}

Note in the Fig 2b table, H column: DN32 row has 145, DN40 row has 153 — but the raw table for 2b: rows: DN32: L1=180, H=145, A="G 1 ½ B"; DN40: L1=200/245/300, H=153, A="G2 B". L=97 rowspan 2, W=98 rowspan 2. Yes.

Wait, check 2a: L, H, W rowspans across 3 rows: L=97, H=119, W=98. Yes.

Actually, for Q3/Q1 the "R" in water meter marking "(R) followed by the ratio value" — the unit column "R" is the ratio designation. I'll set unit_symbol null and value 400.
